_comment: Evidence item set for virp-evidence (autopilot/virp_evidence.py). Each item is ONE named read-only command whose signed output is evidence for a control. This file is DATA: adding, removing or re-wording an item is a config edit, never a code change. Installed at /etc/virp/evidence-items.json; the collector falls back to this tracked copy and records which path it used, and that file's sha256, in every result it writes.
_command_policy: Every command MUST classify GREEN at the gate. The collector re-derives the linux driver's GREEN row locally and REFUSES to submit anything that is not exactly `vtysh -c "show <rest>"` with rest limited to [a-z0-9 ./-] (see src/drivers/driver_linux.c, linux_gate_classify). That local guard exists because this file is operator-editable: an edit must not be able to turn a read-only collector into something that mutates a device. The gate remains the authority — the guard only stops the collector from ever asking.
_caveat_policy: proves / does_not_prove are rendered verbatim into the report next to the signed result. Write them honestly: an evidence collector that overstates what a read demonstrates is worse than no collector at all. Where FRR genuinely cannot evidence a control, say so in evidence_gap and the report marks that control UNEVIDENCED instead of showing a weak read as if it had passed.

items.name: access_accounts
items.title: Configured user accounts and access lines
items.proves: The FRR configuration exactly as the device reports it, including any `username`, `line vty` or `access-class` stanzas that are configured. On a device carrying none of them, this is positive evidence that FRR itself defines no local accounts and no vty access list.
items.does_not_prove: FRR exposes no dedicated account or access-line read — `show users`, `show line` and `show vty` are all rejected as unknown commands by FRR 10.2 — so this is the running-config and the operator must read the account stanzas out of it. It does NOT show the host or container OS accounts (/etc/passwd), SSH authorized keys, sudo policy or PAM configuration, and those are what actually govern who can reach vtysh at all; none of them is reachable from any GREEN gate read. An empty result means no FRR-level user stanza exists, NOT that nobody can log in.

items.name: logging_config
items.title: Logging configuration and target
items.proves: Each running FRR daemon's logging configuration as that daemon reports it at collection time: the syslog, stdout and file destinations and whether each is enabled, the protocol name, record-priority setting and timestamp precision.
items.does_not_prove: Does not prove that any log record was actually written, delivered to a collector, retained for any required period, or reviewed by anyone. It covers the FRR daemons only: the container's own syslog/journald, and any host-level log forwarding, are outside this read.

items.name: time_sync
items.title: Time synchronisation configuration
items.proves: The zebra daemon's own reported wall-clock timestamps (daemon start time and last RIB sweep) — that is, what the device believes the time is.
items.does_not_prove: FRR has no time-synchronisation subsystem and exposes no NTP read at all: `show ntp status`, `show ntp associations` and `show clock` are all unknown commands in FRR 10.2 (verified live against frr1 on 2026-07-30). This read therefore CANNOT evidence a time-sync control. It is a device-reported clock value and nothing more — it does not name a time source, prove synchronisation happened, or bound clock offset. Time sync on these nodes is a host/container concern (chrony, ntpd or systemd-timesyncd) and reading it needs a shell command that the linux gate classifies RED by absence.
items.evidence_gap: FRR exposes no NTP or time-synchronisation configuration through any GREEN vtysh read. This control is UNEVIDENCED by this collector and needs a host-level collector that does not yet exist.

items.name: running_config_baseline
items.title: Running-configuration snapshot for baseline conformance
items.proves: A point-in-time snapshot of the complete running configuration, signed and chain-registered, suitable for later comparison against an approved baseline.
items.does_not_prove: Does not by itself prove baseline conformance: this collector records the configuration, it does not compare it. Baseline comparison and drift alerting are the config-backup runbook's job (docs/RUNBOOK-CONFIG-BACKUP.md). It is also the RUNNING configuration, not the startup configuration — `show startup-config` returns empty on these nodes — so it does not prove what the device would load after a restart. It shares a collection method with the access-accounts item; the two controls are evidenced by the same read, collected and signed independently.

items.name: management_services
items.title: Enabled management services and insecure-protocol posture
items.proves: Which FRR daemons are actually running on the device at collection time, as reported by the running vtysh.
items.does_not_prove: Does not enumerate the host's listening network services or open ports, and therefore does not prove that insecure management protocols (telnet, cleartext HTTP, SNMPv1/v2c) are disabled. The container's sshd — the actual management path VIRP itself uses to reach this device — is not an FRR daemon and does not appear here. A real insecure-protocol posture check needs a host-level port/service read, which no GREEN vtysh row can perform.
